## Client/server import boundary

A `"use client"` module under `app/` or `components/` must never take a value import on `server/**`, whether directly or through a chain of other modules. A value import pulls the server module, and any secret it reads, into the browser bundle. Types are erased at build time, so `import type { Shape } from "@/server/config"` is the permitted shape for anything a client needs to know about a server module.

dependency-cruiser enforces this with two rules in `.dependency-cruiser.cjs`:

- `no-client-to-server-secret` flags a client module whose own import statement targets `server/**`.
- `no-client-to-server-secret-transitive` flags a client module that reaches `server/**` through one or more non-client helpers.

### Running the gate

From `apps/web-platform`:

```bash
bash scripts/constraint-gates.sh
```

Exit 0 means no violation beyond the committed baseline (`.dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json`). Any other exit means either a real boundary violation or a broken toolchain, and both fail closed. The runner cruises `app/`, `components/` and `server/` and matches imports by their resolved path, so all three directories must exist and the `@/*` alias in `tsconfig.json` must resolve.

### What happens when it trips

The `constraint-gates` workflow runs on every pull request that touches `apps/web-platform`. When the gate trips, the pull request shows a red check. When the offending import can be corrected mechanically, the two-stage recovery workflow (ADR-074) opens a draft follow-up pull request carrying the fix for review and merge. When it cannot, the check stays red until the import is changed or the agent refreshes the baseline.

### Proven to bite

Installing this gate did not stop at writing files. The scaffold checked out the committed tree in a detached worktree, ran the gate (pass), injected a direct client import and a one-hop chain into `server/**`, confirmed the gate named each rule on its own edge (fail), removed the probes and ran the gate again (pass). The same proof runs on every `--refresh-baseline`, so a config edit that quietly disarms a rule is caught at the next refresh rather than at the next leak.

### Ownership and recovery

`.dependency-cruiser.cjs`, `scripts/constraint-gates.sh` and the baseline file are agent-owned; do not hand-edit them. To re-baseline after `main` has moved, or to re-run the bite proof, run the `soleur:constraint-scaffold` skill with `--refresh-baseline`. It refuses a dirty tree and captures the baseline against the `origin/main` merge-base, so a leak introduced on the current branch is never grandfathered.
